articles.title: Arjun Prasad turns promise into IGPL title, Ganapathy finishes runner-up
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Arjun Prasad did not have to wait long for his first Indian Golf Premier League title.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Arjun Prasad did not have to wait long for his first Indian Golf Premier League title. Just his second appearance on the IGPL and his first in India was enough for the young professional to turn promise into a trophy at the \ IGPL Invitational 2026 presented at Qutab Golf Course in New Delhi.Prasad, representing Unico Gurugram Tuskers GC, who won the team event, produced the round of the tournament when it mattered most, firing a brilliant seven-under 63 in the third round to finish at 16-under 194. The effort gave him a four-shot cushion over another of the league's emerging young stars, Veer Ganapathy, who was representing the Bengaluru Stallions and finished runner-up at 12-under 198.The victory was built on three rounds of controlled golf—66, 65, and 63—but it was the manner in which Prasad handled the final stretch that underlined his composure. He turned in 31 and came home in 32, making seven birdies without dropping a shot. A run of three consecutive birdies on the front nine, followed by two more on the back nine and birdies at the 17th and 18th, allowed him to pull away from a field packed with established names."Competition is pretty high over here as well. We have some outstanding players who have done phenomenally well internationally," Prasad said after his victory. "I just kept it very simple from the very first day, just kept on following the process, and I'm grateful that I was able to do it all three days and get on top.""The course is playing very differently from what we are generally used to. The fairways are softer, and the greens were soft as well, but the rough was extremely high, and the greens were slower, so it was tough to judge that. Hitting the ball on the fairway and then getting it onto the green was very important. If you missed the green, then those up-and-downs were very tough to make,” Prasad said.Prasad's charge also came at the expense of an intriguing battle involving Ganapathy, who had shared the lead after the second round and was among the players expected to challenge for the title. The Bengaluru youngster carded a 63 of his own in the third round and finished at 12-under 198, four shots behind Prasad.For Ganapathy, the week was another reminder of his growing presence on the IGPL stage. After rounds of 68 and 67, he produced his best golf when the pressure was highest, attacking from the outset and giving himself a chance to stay in the title race."The course is, of course, amazing and in good condition. I mean, it's scoring, but at the same time you have to keep the ball in play, which is important," Ganapathy said. "I think the first two days I struggled a bit, but then I came back well, and I finished well. Today from the start, it was like I was just trying to go as low as I could, and a few putts fell, a few good shots, and yeah, it was a good week."Prasad, who had made his IGPL debut in Ras Al Khaimah in the United Arab Emirates only a couple of weeks earlier, acknowledged that Ganapathy's presence near the top added another layer to the final-round challenge."I'm so happy for the young guy. He played so well," Prasad said. "I had the opportunity to play with him on day one as well, and he's an extremely gritty young kid who has a lot of potential. Having him move up the leaderboard was a great motivation for me to do my best and improve.”Experience also played a role in Prasad's victory. He said a series of top-10 finishes and near misses over the previous season had helped him understand how to handle the critical moments better."Last year I had a lot of top-10 finishes, and I came close. I could only close it one time," he said. "The way I was talking to myself in the round and the kind of headspace I was in, I think that's a lot of experience in it as well. All those things last year and even this year have come together for this thing."Behind the leading duo, RVR Delhi Blue Bulls captain Shiv Kapur finished third at 11-under 199 after a final-round 65. Four-time IGPL winner Gaganjeet Bhullar carded a five-under final round to finish fourth at 10-under 200, while Olympian Udayan Mane, Karandeep Kochhar, and Harshjeet Sethie shared fifth place.The tournament had a strong women's presence too, with Kashika Misra finishing as the leading woman golfer. After taking the lead with rounds of 66 and 64, Misra carded a six-over 76 on the final day and finished tied 20th. Her performance over the first two rounds, however, had put her firmly at the center of the tournament narrative.Ganapathy was among those impressed by the young golfer. "She's played incredible golf the whole week. She was literally destroying us, I would say," he said. "All respect to her. It's not that easy, and coming out here and beating all the men is tough. Props to her."The mixed field was one of the aspects Ganapathy felt made the IGPL different from conventional golf tournaments.The team competition added another dimension. Unico Gurugram Tuskers, powered by Prasad's title-winning performance, finished on 23-under to claim team honours. Shat Mishra, Tushar Pannu, and Shaurya Binu completed the winning combination, with the Tuskers finishing four shots ahead of Vimtra Chennai Lions GC, who were second at 19-under. Gaganjeet Bhullar's fourth-place finish and Harshjeet Sethie's tied-fifth effort led the Lions' challenge.Five teams, Bengaluru Stallions, Flying Man Kolkata, Auro Goa Eagles, RVR Delhi Blue Bulls, and Punjab Raptors shared third place at 18-under.For Ganapathy, the team element has become an important part of the league's appeal."IGPL introducing the team format is something new, and I think it's a great thing because now it becomes like a camaraderie between the four players," he said. "Keeping our placements aside, we have a really good bond on and off the course."Prasad echoed that sentiment after helping the Tuskers secure the team title."This week I was playing for the Gurugram Tuskers, and I think the camaraderie is something I'm getting the hang of. It's new, and it's exciting," he said.At Qutab, however, it was Prasad who had the final word. His 63 transformed a close contest into a decisive victory and gave the IGPL another new champion in an increasingly competitive season.For a player who arrived in the league only weeks ago, the breakthrough could hardly have been louder: three rounds, 16-under par and a trophy to show for it.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: Matthew Jordan moves into contention with Casey Jarvis leading by one
articles.summary: Matthew Jordan survives 'sledging' from outspoken television presenter Piers Morgan to move into contention at Alfred Dunhill Links; South African Casey Jarvis leads by one on 11 under after a 67 at Kingsbarns
articles.body:
The Royal Liverpool member is looking for his first DP World Tour win in his 183rd tournament and he shrugged off the good-natured criticism from the television presenter - his amateur playing partner for the team part of the event - to card six birdies and an eagle at Carnoustie.

His one mishap was a bogey at the ninth, his final hole, but he got to 10 under and into a four-way tie for second place.

"Yeah, with Piers, the amount of sledging that goes on towards me is incredible," said Jordan.

"We are supposed to be a team but honestly it's all about him and that's how he makes it.

"I think Peter Jones (star of Dragons Den) missed a two-foot putt on 15 and he (Morgan) comes up to me - because I hit it to two foot as well - and he says: 'Don't do a Jonesy'.

"So that kind of puts the heebie-jeebies in you over that small putt. He just cuts at me like that and every time I seem to do something good, it's him taking the limelight."

South African Casey Jarvis leads by one on 11 under after a 67 at Kingsbarns but the round of the delay belonged to Spaniard Rocco Repetto Taylor who had an eight-under 64 at Kingsbarns, the second of three courses being used for the first three rounds with St Andrews also hosting on the final day.

The 23-year-old had four birdies and an eagle in his final nine holes to sit 10 under alongside Jordan and South African MJ Daffue.

Defending champion Bob MacIntyre is at eight under after a 65 at Kingsbarns, where Brooks Koepka shot a 67 to sit level with the Scot.

Tommy Fleetwood is at six under after a four-under 68 at Kingsbarns, as is Ryder Cup team-mate Matt Fitzpatrick with a 70 at the same course.

In their first DP World Tour appearances in nearly four years, Lee Westwood got to four under after a 69 at Kingsbarns but fellow LIV golfer Ian Poulter went out in 41 at Carnoustie on his way to 76 which left him four over.

articles.title: Sustainable construction, effective pollution control need of the hour, says MahaMetro MD Hardikar
articles.summary: MahaMetro MD Shravan Hardikar urges sustainable construction and stricter dust control at GRIHA Regional Conclave 2026 in Pune; MoUs signed with colleges.
articles.body: Pune: Sustainable and environment-friendly construction practices are essential to address the environmental impact of rapid urbanisation, Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation managing director Shravan Hardikar said at the inauguration of GRIHA Regional Conclave 2026 in Pune on Wednesday.Speaking at the event, organised by GRIHA (Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment) Council, which is jointly established by Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE) and The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI), and Sustainability Initiative (SI), Hardikar said effective implementation of environmental regulations, regular monitoring and adoption of sustainable construction practices were necessary to control pollution from the construction sector.“If sustainable development is to be achieved, everyone needs to take the initiative. Those who do not adopt environment-friendly construction practices should face punitive action. With construction activity increasing across cities, dust pollution is also rising, making effective implementation of dust-control measures essential,” Hardikar said.The conclave, held at Hotel Conrad in Koregaon Park, was themed ‘Pathways for a Low Carbon Future: Building to Infrastructure’. It brought together architects, developers, infrastructure experts, govt officials, academics and sustainability professionals to discuss low-carbon buildings, resilient infrastructure, climate finance and sustainable urban development.A key highlight of the inaugural session was the signing of two MoUs. GRIHA signed an MoU with Vishwakarma University, Pune, with GRIHA CEO Sanjay Seth and Dr Priti Dhanwat, Dean, School of Architecture and Planning, Vishwakarma University, exchanging the agreement. A second MoU was signed with Dr D. Y. Patil College of Architecture, Mumbai, and was exchanged by Shabnam Bassi, Director, Sustainable Buildings Division, TERI, and Prof Dinesh Zope.Prof Sunil S. Bhagwat, Director, IISER Pune, said India could potentially take a leadership role globally in sustainability in the coming years. “Sustainability is important, but economics and human needs are equally significant. There is a need for extensive research and innovative initiatives to achieve environment-friendly and sustainable development,” he said.Sanjay Seth said Pune is a rapidly growing city, and it needs infrastructure to support its rapid growth, but such development should not come at the cost of the environment. “All stakeholders need to work together to promote sustainable and environment-friendly construction. The conclave can provide direction for such collaborative efforts,” he said.The event began with a fireside chat with environmental experts Dr Prasad Modak and Ar. Anagha Paranjape-Purohit. Projects and schools that had received GRIHA ratings were also felicitated. A GRIHA delegation also visited Saarthi, a green building in Pune, as part of the programme.The plenary session on ‘Scaling Sustainability: From Green Buildings to Resilient Cities and Infrastructure’ examined ways to reduce energy, carbon, water and resource consumption through sustainable building practices. Another roundtable session, on ‘Moving Towards Low Carbon Transition: Business Strategy, Climate Finance and Building Stakeholder Capacity to Derive Carbon Value’, discussed green finance, business strategies, carbon markets and the economic potential of verified emission reductions.The conclave was attended by GRIHA CEO Sanjay Seth, TERI’s Shabnam Bassi, IISER Pune Director Prof Sunil Bhagwat, Dr Prasad Modak, VK Group Chairman & Managing Director Hrishikesh Kulkarni, former PMRDA chief engineer Vivek Kharwadkar, Developer Sarvesh Javadekar, Architect Anuja Pandit, Sustainability Initiative trustee Ar. Anagha Paranjape-Purohit, Upendra Deshpande, Vijay Sane, Prof. Dinesh Zope and Dr Priti Dhanwat, among others. articles.title: Ravens Announce Lamar Jackson News Ahead of Week 4 Titans Game
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens have made final rulings on several players for their Week 4 showdown with the Tennessee Titans.It was already announced by Ravens head c...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens have made final rulings on several players for their Week 4 showdown with the Tennessee Titans.

It was already announced by Ravens head coach Jesse Minter that edge rusher Trey Hendrickson was going to be out after getting a procedure done on his finger. That left other questions about the roster going into the game.

Baltimore released its last injury report before the Titans game. It answered some big questions, including the status of quarterback Lamar Jackson after he dealt with a back injury that limited him earlier in the week.

Baltimore Ravens Reveal Lamar Jackson's Status for the Titans Game

After some health concerns, Jackson is officially good to go with his back injury, as he did not have an injury designation. His fellow offensive players, Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ronnie Stanley (toe), were listed as questionable.

Last season, Jackson missed at least one practice a week, but only because he was playing hurt. This suggests he is officially good to play and will be on the field barring any major setbacks before kickoff.

This season, Jackson has thrown for 745 yards and 4 touchdowns to 1 interception . He's added another 124 yards and 1 touchdown on the ground.

Lamar Jackson Officially Good to Go for Ravens vs. Titans

This is a massive relief for Ravens fans to see that Jackson is good to go. Last year, he missed multiple games with all kinds of injuries. That really set the franchise back; losing him again is something they don't want to repeat in 2026.

The real question is whether Jackson will have his top receiver, Flowers, and his top offensive lineman, Stanley, on the field. Those two are critical to the team's success if the Ravens want to win.

Losing Hendrickson is already a big blow, but the team has at least some depth at edge rusher. Tavius Robinson will be the top pass rusher, with Mike Green and rookie Zion Young getting more reps on the field.

Stanley might be the more important player to get back on the field with the offensive line issues. Both Ravens centers have been ruled out, putting rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane in line for his first career start at center.

The winless Titans should be a winnable game for the Ravens, but injuries could hold them back. It's a good thing that Jackson is available, as he will be the key to a Baltimore win. If he can help carry this offense and get the running game going with Derrick Henry, this should be a 3-1 start for them.

articles.title: Tom Kim gains exemption from South Korea’s military service after securing Asian Games gold medal
articles.summary: Tom Kim claimed a three-shot victory in the Men's Individual Strokeplay event to secure gold at the Asian Games and exempt him from completing full mandatory military service; watch Kim in action throughout the PGA Tour season, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 24-year-old took a one-shot lead heading into the final round, but carded a sensational six-under 64 to secure gold and finish three shots clear of Japan's Higa Kazuki, China's Wenyi Ding and Sadom Kaewkanjana of Thailand.

Kim top-scored for the International Team at last week's Presidents Cup against Team USA before making an immediate trip to Japan, where he was among three South Korean male golfers to feature at Kasugai Country Club.

South Korean men must enlist in the military by the age of 28, serving for 18-21 months, but an Asian Games gold medal or Olympic medal provides an exemption from full military service.

The four-time PGA Tour winner, who won the Genesis Scottish Open in July, needed to win either the individual or team event to secure that exemption and, effectively, avoid having to pause his golfing career.

A gold medal means Kim will now be able to undergo basic military training, which lasts less than a month, similar to former Tottenham captain Heung-Min Son, who completed a three-week basic military training camp in 2020 after he led South Korea to gold at the Asian Games in 2018.

"It's unbelievable," Kim said. "I had one goal, and to be able to represent Korea and to win the gold medal, it's something that I will never forget in my career."

Kim partnered with Seonghyeon Kim and Doyeob Mun for the team event. The South Korean trio entered the final round one shot clear at the top of the leaderboard, but would finish two shots behind China in second.

Kim got off to an excellent start during Saturday's final round, going four under on his front nine, with birdies on holes two, four, six and eight.

He added another on the 11th, before extending his lead to 19 under with an eagle on the 13th hole.

A bogey on the 17th set him back to 18 under, but Kim would make par on the last to secure his spot at the top of the podium.

His compatriot Mun placed tied for eighth at eight under par, while fellow South Korean, Seonghyeon Kim, tied-24th at one over par.

Kim previously tried to secure his exemption at the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he finished four shots outside the bronze-medal position. The 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles would have been his last opportunity before the age limit.

Sungjae Im and Si Woo Kim took team gold in the 2023 Asian Games, earning their military exemptions, although Sangmoon Bae - part of the 2015 Presidents Cup team - is among the golfers to have seen their career disrupted by military service .

articles.title: 'I like being the first to do things': Meet Pranavi Urs, who made history with Asian Games golf gold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Pranavi Urs made history at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, becoming the first Indian woman golfer to win an individual gold medal
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pranavi Urs made history at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, becoming the first Indian woman golfer to win an individual gold medal at the Games.The 23-year-old from Mysuru held her nerve in a tense final round to finish one stroke ahead of the field. Her victory also helped India win the women's team silver medal.Pranavi finished the four-day competition at 15-under 265, with a final-round score of even-par 70.Triple bogey, then a strong comebackPranavi began the final round with a three-stroke lead but saw her advantage disappear after a triple bogey on the third hole. She responded strongly, making three birdies on the sixth, 10th and 13th holes to get back in control. She then held on to her one-stroke lead to complete a historic victory.China's Yin Ruoning won silver after shooting 67 in the final round. She finished at 14-under 266.Singapore's Shannon Tan also ended at 266 after a 68. She won the bronze medal following a playoff.'The first will always be the first'Pranavi was delighted after completing the biggest victory of her career."I like being the first to do things," a jubilant Pranavi said after the historic triumph."People will come along to do more but the first will always be the first," she said.Her victory ended a long wait for India in Asian Games golf.Pranavi's gold was India's first golfing gold since Shiv Kapur won the men's individual title in 2002. It was also India's best performance in golf since the 1982 Delhi Asian Games, when golf became part of the Games programme.Lakshman Singh won the men's individual gold that year. He was also part of India's gold-winning team alongside Amit Luthra and Rajiv Mohta.Pranavi helps India win team silverPranavi's individual gold was followed by a team silver for India.The Indian women's team consisted of Pranavi, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar. The two best scores from the three golfers were counted for the team competition.India finished with a combined score of 14-under 546, behind gold medallists China, who finished at 22-under 538.Aditi produced her best round of the week, shooting 67. She made five consecutive birdies but also had a double bogey and a bogey. She finished tied 14th in the individual event at 2-over 282.Diksha shot 77 in the final round and finished tied 23rd with a total of 12-over.The result gave India its best-ever performance in the women's team golf event at the Asian Games.Who is Pranavi Urs?Pranavi Sharath Urs was born on April 15, 2003, in Mysuru, Karnataka. She started playing golf as a child after watching her father and brother play at the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar Golf Club in Mysuru.She made her mark in junior golf, winning the 2018 Singha World Junior Championship in Thailand and the All India Junior Girls Championship.Pranavi turned professional in 2020 and competed on the domestic women's professional golf circuit before moving to the international stage.She represented India at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023, finishing 13th in the individual event and fourth in the team event.From domestic golf to the international stagePranavi has competed on the Ladies European Tour (LET) and produced several notable results. She finished third at the Andalucía Costa del Sol Open de España in 2024 and tied for third at the Dormy Open Helsingborg that year. She also finished fourth at the Hero Women's Indian Open 2025 and tied for fifth at the Lacoste Ladies Open de France 2025.In 2025, she won the IGPL Invitational Mumbai, becoming the first Indian woman to win a professional open-field tournament featuring male golfers.She finished 17th in the 2024 Ladies European Tour standings during her first full season on the tour.Pranavi was also conferred the Arjuna Award in 2023 for her achievements and contribution to Indian golf.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Golfer Tom Kim wins gold to secure military service exemption
articles.summary: Golfer Tom Kim wins gold at the Asian Games to secure an exemption from mandatory service in South Korea's military.
articles.body:
18 T Kim (Kor); -15 K Higa (Jpn), W Ding (Chi), S Kaewkanjana (Tha); -11 W-H Wang (Tpe)

Tom Kim won gold at the Asian Games to secure an exemption from mandatory service in South Korea's military.

The 24-year-old led going into the final round and produced a brilliant six-under-par 64 to finish 18 under and claim victory by three strokes.

There were signs of nerves with a bogey on the 17th but, after five birdies and an eagle prior to that, Kim had the margin for error and tapped in for par on the last before letting out a roar, his relief clear to see.

Able-bodied South Korean males are usually required to undertake between 18 and 21 months of military service before the age of 28.

However, the government rewards Asian Games champions and Olympic medal-winners of any colour with a service exemption bar basic training, which lasts less than a month.

Athletes who have previously secured the exemption include former Tottenham footballer Son Heung-min, who served for only three weeks in 2020 having won the Asian Games with his country two years earlier.

Kim rushed from the Presidents Cup in the United States to tee off at the Kasugai Country Club in Japan, having to manage on just six hours of sleep and a 14-hour time difference.

His efforts were worth it as the world number 32 can now continue his career, in which he has already won four PGA Tour titles and triumphed at the Scottish Open in July, with minimal disruption.

Kim had previously come close to securing an exemption at the Paris Olympics in 2024, finishing day one tied for third before ultimately finishing eighth.

However, his compatriot SH Kim, 28, missed out on a military exemption as South Korea could only win silver in the team event, alongside Tom Kim and Mun Do-yeob, who has already completed his service.

articles.title: Tom Kim se libra de la mili tras ganar el oro en los Juegos Asiáticos
articles.standfirst: Su apresurada salida de la Presidents Cup le ha salido rentable al ganar el torneo de golf de la competición asiática que le permite quedar exento del servicio militar surcoreano
articles.summary: Su apresurada salida de la Presidents Cup le ha salido rentable al ganar el torneo de golf de la competición asiática que le permite quedar exento del servicio militar surcoreano
articles.body: el surcoreano Tom Kim se marchó a toda prisa de la Presidents Cup sin esperar a ver si finalmente Japón se imponía a Estados Unidos. Había acabado su partido individual, el segundo de la jornada dominical, y firmado el cuarto punto que daba a su equipo. La celeridad por abandonar Medinah (Chicago) se debía a su participación en los Juegos Asiáticos. El torneo de golf arrancaba tres días después en el Kasugai Country Club (Kasugai, prefectura de Aichi, Japón). Y ganar el oro tenía un premio de lo más atractivo: librarse del servicio militar obligatorio. Kim se hubiera perdido la celebración de Japón si hubiera ganado una competición que se le resiste desde hace 28 años. Los estadounidenses remontaron y se llevaron el triunfo por 17-13. En cambio, su precipitada salida encontró recompensa en Japón. El número 32 del mundo se llevó la victoria con 262 golpes y 18 bajo par tras una gran última vuelta de 64 (-6) para imponerse con tres golpes de ventaja sobre el japonés Kazuki Higa, que terminó con -15. El golfista surcoreano, con 13 triunfos profesionales, cuatro de ellos en el PGA Tour, se libra de este modo de los casi dos años de servicio militar obligatorio que deben cumplir todos los hombres, salvo contadas excepciones. El período de tiempo al servicio del ejército va de 18 a 21 meses. Las exenciones especiales quedan limitadas a artistas o deportistas que destacan en competiciones internacionales vinculadas al prestigio nacional. En el caso de los deportistas surcoreanos, una medalla en los Juegos Olímpicos (Kim rozó el bronce en París 2024 al acabar a cuatro golpes del tercer puesto), pero se quedó o un oro individual o por equipos en los Juegos Asiáticos permite no realizar la mili. Kim sí deberá completar la formación militar básica y quedará encuadrado como personal deportivo durante 34 meses. Durante ese periodo deberá completar 544 horas de servicio comunitario relacionado con el deporte.

articles.title: Falcons Honeymooners Face Tough Test In New Orleans Dome
articles.summary: Falcons honeymooners head to New Orleans for the Domecoming. Can Atlanta handle the noise and the history? The stats say it will be brutal.
articles.body:
Two Falcons fans are spending their honeymoon in New Orleans this week. They picked the one game in Atlanta's schedule that matters most to the city. This isn't just a date. It is a trip to the Superdome for the 20th anniversary of the Saints' return after Hurricane Katrina. The atmosphere will be thick with history and hate for the visiting team. While the couple celebrates, the Falcons must survive a hostile crowd that has not forgotten 20 years of rivalry.

New Orleans is not a normal road game. The Superdome creates a pressure cooker that breaks visiting teams. Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski knows this reality better than anyone. He told reporters that "In this league, you go on the road; you get to experience some incredible crowds." That sounds polite. The truth is much darker for Atlanta. The Saints are 1-2, but they have played close games. The Falcons are also 1-2, yet they have been erratic. One week they get crushed 34-3 to Carolina, the next they beat the Packers. That inconsistency is a death sentence in a place like this.

Old rivals want to turn the Falcons into "Trashlanta." Long-time Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan said, "You know the importance of this game," before adding, "'Can'tlanta' comes to the dome. We have to turn them into 'Trashlanta.'" That is not a friendly jab. It is a promise of pain. The Falcons have to deal with the emotional weight of a city that feels like a family reunion gone wrong.

Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has one job: keep his head up. He handled the Green Bay crowd well in his last start. Stefanski praised him, noting, "Mike did an outstanding job both in the huddle and at the line of scrimmage the other night, and getting us in and out of the correct plays, making adjustments when necessary." The stats back this up. Penix threw for 256 yards. Bijan Robinson ran for 194 yards and two touchdowns. Drake London caught nine passes for 194 yards. These are huge numbers. But numbers from Green Bay mean nothing in New Orleans.

The Saints have a run defense that ranks 27th in the league. They are weak against the run. Yet the Falcons are 29th in pass defense themselves. This is a trap. The Saints will throw deep with Tyler Shough and Chris Olave. They are third in the NFL in passing offense. If Penix slips up, the crowd will eat him alive. The Falcons need to lean on their best unit. They are second in rushing and have the best run defense in the league. They gave up just 47.7 yards per game. They held the Packers to 17 rushing yards. That is the only way to win.

New Orleans is not invincible. They lost their home opener to Las Vegas 35-27. They squandered an 11-point lead and turned the ball over four times. Tight end Juwan Johnson tried to calm fans, saying, "We've only played three games. It's nothing to panic over." He claimed the team is "playing really aggressive, really strong, really physical, really smart and really fast." But mistakes cost them. All three are 1-2, but Carolina currently holds the division lead on tiebreakers. Every game is a must-win.

The Saints also lost their top rusher, Travis Etienne Jr., to a hamstring injury. He is out for at least four weeks. They will rely on Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. Coach Kellen Moore said, "We feel fortunate that we have Alvin." But the offense still needs to protect the ball. The Falcons have the tools to exploit a messy Saints team. The question is if they can handle the noise. The couple on their honeymoon will see a packed house. The Falcons will see a wall of sound. They must block it out.

articles.title: How Tony Romo got on while playing PGA Tour Q-School event
articles.summary: Tony Romo is still trying to crack the world of professional golf. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback is an exceptional golfer.
articles.body:
Tony Romo is still trying to crack the world of professional golf. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback is an exceptional golfer. His handicap is around +3, and he regularly dominates high-profile celebrity events, winning the American Century Championship multiple times.

However, when he tests his game against professional fields through sponsor exemptions on the PGA Tour and Korn Ferry Tour, the gap between elite amateurs and touring professionals becomes apparent.

He shot a 77 in his PGA Tour debut and has consistently missed the cut in professional tournaments. Under the bright lights of the PGA Tour, even minor holes in your game get exposed.

He recently went through pre-qualifying at Q-School in Oklahoma, and once again it didn't quite go to plan.

How Tony Romo performed in Q-School pre-qualifying event

Romo's pre-qualifying event in Oklahoma looked promising for a while. The 46-year-old was in contention to make it into the top 37 and advance through the pre-qualifying stage. He was T46 with nine holes to play after a birdie on the ninth.

However, it all came undone. Romo shot a 74 in his third and final round to finish nine-over par, four shots above the cutline as play concluded. It was a disappointing end to what could have been a huge success for Romo.

Romo has competed in PGA Tour Q-School pre-qualifying five times and has played in several PGA Tour tournaments with a sponsor's exemption. He's also tried to qualify for the US Open several times to no avail.

But to make matters worse, while he was competing in Oklahoma, CBS announced it was parting ways with Romo, who previously commentated on their NFL coverage. Romo was arrested in late July for a DUI while leaving the Wisconsin Amateur Golf Championship.

CBS initially placed Romo on leave for the start of the NFL season, but has now made the move permanent by officially cutting ties with the former Cowboys star.

They said in a statement: "CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways. We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward."

So it didn't go his way on the course, and CBS let him go off the course. A poor day all round for Romo.

articles.title: Greens would offer two-year jobs to unemployed under-24s
articles.summary: Co-deputy leader Mothin Ali tells the party's conference many young people are "bored, desperate and lost".
articles.body:
Young people would be offered a guaranteed two-year job within four months of leaving education or training, under a new proposal unveiled by the Green Party.

Announcing the policy at the party's conference in Brighton, co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said there were a million "bored, desperate and lost" young people who were out of work, training or education.

Under the proposed scheme, youngsters would be offered posts in the private sector, with the government paying half their salary.

The Greens have not specified a budget for the policy, but have argued it would reduce spending on welfare and boost tax receipts from employment.

The party says it would initially target the plan in areas with the fewest jobs openings for young people, citing Rotherham, Ceredigion, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Broxtowe and South Staffordshire, with an ambition to roll it out nationwide.

Employers would be exempt from paying National Insurance contributions, but would have to provide in-job training, the party says.

The party is seeking to pitch the plan as more ambitious than the government's own scheme, which subsidises six-month job placements for benefit claimants who have been looking for work for 18 months.

Ali also criticised ministers for previously suggesting youngsters refusing a role under that scheme could lose access to benefits, telling activists: "Threatening young people with cuts to Universal Credit if they don't accept short-term work placements - that's not a youth strategy."

He added: "Working class kids should be able to dream. But more than dream, they should have a genuine chance of making those dreams a reality.

The number of 16-24-year-olds who are not in employment, education or training has been rising since the Covid pandemic, with figures reaching almost one million.

A long-awaited report into the problem by former Labour minister Alan Milburn is expected to be published this autumn.

What does Neet stand for and why does the UK have so many?

Greens can move Labour in the right direction, says Polanski

In her own speech to the conference, Ali's fellow co-deputy leader Rachel Millward said the Greens would immediately bring both Thames Water and South East Water back into public ownership.

She argued this could be done without paying compensation to shareholders, pointing to water supply problems and a lack of new reservoirs.

Andy Burnham has promised to bring water under greater public control, but has stopped short of announcing plans to nationalise any water companies.

Millward told the conference the prime minister was "making a mistake" and his "10-year plan of gentle threats and vague notions of control is not enough".

"We need public ownership now, and we have all the tools we need to make it happen," she said.

South East Water said it was "focused on delivering on our commitments by investing £1.9 billion into local infrastructure and resilience over the next five years.

"We support working closely with the communities we serve and are accountable to, so that we can provide the best possible service for customers".

Thames Water has been approached for a response.

articles.title: Tom Kim wins gold at Asian Games, secures exemption from South Korea military service
articles.summary: Kim shot 6-under-par in the final round to win by three strokes.
articles.body:
Tom Kim's 6-under-par final round of the Asian Games on Saturday helped secure a gold medal and an exemption from South Korea's mandatory military service.

The win was the payoff for Kim, who left the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club last Sunday in Chicago to fly to Japan to compete in the tournament at Kasugai Country Club. He landed at 5 a.m. Tuesday and participated in a practice round three hours later while jet-lagged.

"It did not even feel like I had a tournament starting the next day," Kim said .

Able-bodied South Korean men are required to take on 18-21 months of military service before they turn 28. The government hands out exemptions to winners of Asian Games events and those who take home an Olympic medal of any color. Kim fell short at the 2024 Paris Olympics when he finished eighth in men's golf.

The 24-year-old Kim finished the 2026 Asian Games 18-under-par to win the event by three strokes. His last opportunity at an exemption had he not won this week was likely the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, when he would be 26.

"I came here believing that if I just did my thing, things would work out well in the end," Kim said. "I tried to maintain that mindset throughout and just play my game."

Kim was inspired on Saturday after waking up to a text message from golf legend and TGL teammate Tiger Woods saying , "Just be you. Nothing more, nothing less."

A reply has not been sent just yet, but Kim said, "I think I will send him a photo of me biting my gold medal."

articles.title: PGA Tour Golfer Exempt from Military Service After Winning Gold Medal at Asian Games
articles.summary: PGA Tour golfer Tom Kim has been exempt from mandatory military service in South Korea after winning gold at the Asian Games, according to the AP's Stephen Wade.
articles.body:
PGA Tour golfer Tom Kim has been exempt from mandatory military service in South Korea after winning gold at the Asian Games, according to the AP's Stephen Wade .

After heading into the final round with a one-shot lead, Kim shot a 6-under 64 Saturday to finish the tournament at 18-under par.

He will now earn an exemption given to South Korean able-bodied men in honor of accomplishments made while representing their country, including winning any Olympic medal or an Asian Games gold, according to Wade.

Kim had a shot at exemption from military service at the 2024 Paris Olympics but finished four shots outside of medal contention.

This year, he flew to Japan to compete in the Asian Games while the 2026 Presidents Cup was still wrapping up last week in Illinois.

Kim won three of his four Presidents Cup matches before leaving Sunday before the United States clinched a comeback victory over the international team.

Fellow PGA Tour golfer S.H. Kim was also competing in the Asian Games as a member of South Korea's three-man team.

articles.title: Dunhill Links Championship: Casey Jarvis leads going into final round as he seeks third DP World tour title of year
articles.summary: After day three at the Dunhill Links Championship South Africa's Casey Jarvis has a two-shot lead; Jarvis is looking to win his third title this year on the DP World Tour;  Jarvis holed out for eagle on his first hole and with that strong start posted a seven-under 65 on the Old Course
articles.body:
South Africa's Jarvis played bogey-free on a breezy day at the home of golf, and didn't make a birdie putt longer than six feet in keeping his distance against the field.

Jarvis was at 18 under going into the final round.

Adrian Meronk of Poland, one of 22 players from LIV Golf in the field, birdied his opening four holes at Kingsbarns and had an eagle late in his round of 63. He was two shots behind with Matthew Jordan of England, who shot a 66.

Thomas Detry of Belgium, another LIV player, was a further shot back after a 65 at St Andrews.

Jarvis began his round on the 10th hole, and watched his wedge land about six feet beyond the hole and spin back into the cup. He followed that with a tee shot over the Strath bunker to four feet on the par-three 11th. When he two-putted for birdie on the 14th, he already was five under through five holes.

"I know I'm going to be feeling pressure tomorrow," said Jarvis, who won the Kenya Open and South African Open in consecutive weeks in February.

"I have won twice this year so I kind of know how to deal with it a little better. I still know I'm going to feel first tee nerves and pressure throughout the day."

Matt Fitzpatrick, coming off a victory last week in France, also got off to a great start with six birdies in his opening seven holes. He was even par the rest of the way - two birdies to go with two bogeys - for a 66 and wound up six shots behind, along with defending champion Robert MacIntyre.

Five-time major champion Brooks Koepka shot 70 on the Old Course and was eight back.

"Every golfer dreams of taking a lead, playing the Old Course on Sunday," Jarvis said. "I got goosebumps right now just standing here. I just can't wait for tomorrow. Even if I don't win, to be taking the lead, I'm just going to enjoy it as much as I can."

Tyrrell Hatton and Cam Smith, who won the British Open at St Andrews in 2022, were among 14 players from LIV who missed the cut.

Meronk said he plans to play every week he can on the DP World tour with hopes of finishing high enough in the Race to Dubai to secure his card for 2027 and keep his options open depending on what happens with LIV.

"I've been playing really well the last couple of weeks. Just didn't get the full results," Meronk said. "Hopefully, this is the week. But just play my game tomorrow and see what happens at the end."

articles.title: 2026 Baycurrent Classic field: Tom Kim withdraws from Yokohama after Asian Games win

articles.body:
The PGA Tour heads to Yokohama Country Club in Japan next week, where an $8 million purse and 500 FedExCup points are at stake.

Xander Schauffele returns as the defending champion following a strong outing representing the U.S. at Medinah. He closed with a 64 last October to hold off Max Greyserman by one stroke for his 10th PGA Tour title .

The Baycurrent Classic, the third of eight tournaments on the FedExCup Fall schedule , is a 72-player, no-cut field. One of those 72 players — Tom Kim — withdrew from the tournament on Saturday after winning the 2026 Asian Games. Kim, who left the Presidents Cup early and flew from Chicago to Japan for the Asian Games, earned an exemption from South Korea's mandatory military obligation.

Here's who else is scheduled to join Schauffele in Yokohama.

articles.title: 2026 Bank of Utah Championship: Johnny Keefer, Ben James and other young stars go low in desert
articles.summary: Moving Day at Black Desert Resort saw four players 25 years or younger complete bogey-free rounds and move into the top 20 of the leaderboard.
articles.body:
While the Bank of Utah Championship is being led by a pair of Tour veterans in Austin Smotherman and Doug Ghim, it was a quartet of relative newcomers that made the biggest splash on Saturday at the Black Desert Resort.

Johnny Keefer, David Ford, Ben James, and Kihei Akina are all 25 years old or young. All four sit inside the top 20 of the leaderboard , and all four got into the clubhouse with a bogey-free card on Moving Day.

Akina, 20, is the group's lone amateur. After representing the U.S. at the Walker Cup last month , the BYU sophomore opened with 67-67 over the first two rounds in the desert. His start Saturday was pretty unremarkable with four straight pars before he birdied the par-4 14th.

He circled again at the turn and went on to birdie four of five holes in the middle of his final nine holes.

"The whole day I had really solid feels of my approach play, so I was hitting the irons well and giving myself a lot of looks. 5, 6 and 7," he said of a stretch of three straight birdies. "I made really good putts there, and that kind of helped me finish well."

Keefer, the oldest of the group at 25, used an eagle at the par-7th to launch him into a tie for sixth entering Sunday's final round. The 2025 Korn Ferry Tour points list leader posted his second 62 in as many events.

His 9 under on Saturday matches his career low, which was set just two weeks ago during the third round of the Biltmore Championship.

"I feel like the game has been trending really nicely," Keefer told reporters after his round. "First two days I hit the ball off the tee great, and was just kind of waiting for my opportunities. Every now and then the putts would drop, was just kind of real steady, and then today obviously some more putts dropped."

Tune in to the final round of the Bank of Utah Championship at Black Desert Resort in Ivins, Utah.

The Baylor grad said he was looking forward to "go out and hunt" Smotherman and Ghim on Sunday. He sits six shots back of Smotherman's lead at 23 under.

James looked as if he would be tied with Keefer at 17 under but wound up with a birdie at the par-5 18th, circling the course's longest hole to move into a tie for third with Trace Crowe and Kevin Streelman at 18 under.

The 23-year-old Tour rookie made his debut at the RBC Canadian Open in June and his since finished inside the top five three times, including a runner-up at the Biltmore where he shot a final round 61 .

He opened 65-66 in Utah before putting together a blemish-free, 7-under 64.

"Did everything I was supposed to do, hit pretty much every fairway and cleaned up around the green well," the University of Virginia product told Golf Channel's Amy Rogers after his round. "I made a lot of putts inside of eight feet which I needed to do and I didn't make any crazy mistakes."

Ford sits T-9 with three others after posting a 65 — his second such score this week after putting together five birdies, an eagle and a bogey on the opening round on Thursday.

The 24-year-old UNC alum finished inside the top 20 of the American Express and the Puerto Rico Open earlier in the year before taking five months off between April's Valero Texas Open and the Biltmore — the Tour's fall season kick-off.

"I have nothing to lose tomorrow. I'm going to play the best I can, try to hit smart shots, and if the putts fall, great," said James, sounding like his peers who entered the clubhouse earlier with similar low scores. "If not, go on to the next week."

As far as peers are concerned, it is hard for any player in college or who has graduated recently to match the profile of Jackson Koivun.

The 21-year-old Auburn sensation starred for the U.S. at Medinah during the Presidents Cup last week and birdied the final hole Friday to make the cut in Utah.

On Saturday, he birdied three of his final five holes on his first nine before stumbling over his final nine holes.

After bogeys at No. 2 and No. 8, Koivun finished with a 2-under 70 and sits T-61 at 7 under on the tournament.

Five days after helping the U.S. to a Presidents Cup win at Medinah, Jackson Koivun found himself facing the projected cut in Utah. He fought off the nerves with three birdies over his final five holes to reach 6 under and make it to the weekend.

articles.title: Thousands taking part in Great Scottish Run through Glasgow
articles.summary: Organisers predict about 35,000 adults and children will take part in a weekend of events which kicked off on Saturday.
articles.body:
Tens of thousands of people have gathered in Glasgow ahead of this year's Great Scottish Run.

Organisers predict about 35,000 adults and children will take part in a weekend of events which kicked off on Saturday.

Sunday's runs include a 10k and a half marathon, with Scotland's 2022 Commonwealth Games gold medallist Eilish McColgan and charity fundraiser Craig Ferguson the official starters.

Saturday's schedule saw the return of events for junior runners and toddlers, after fears over Storm Amy last year forced them to be cancelled.

What are the Great Scottish Run routes and which roads are closed?

Athena and Hammer from the Gladiators TV show sent off over 2,000 young runners in the AJ Bell Junior and Mini Great Scottish Run on Glasgow Green.

Athena said: "Seeing so many young runners give it everything was brilliant. The energy on Glasgow Green was unreal, and every single one of them should be proud of themselves."

McColgan, who joined the children at the starting line, said: "Days like this are where it all starts. I loved running as a kid, and seeing thousands of children crossing the finish line with huge smiles is the best thing about the Great Scottish Run weekend."

Sunday's action began with the start of the 10k at 08:26.

McColgan, a four times Olympian and Ferguson, known for his kilted trek across the US to Scotland's World Cup opening match this year, will start the proceedings on with elite wheelchair competitors first to go.

Three colour co-ordinated waves of runners then head off for the 10k between 08:30 and 09:03.

The half marathon (13.1 miles) follows later. It will feature six waves of participants with the first, comprising of elite runners, setting the pace at 10:10.

What are the 10k and half marathon routes?

Both the 10k and half marathon start on St Vincent Street in the city centre and conclude on Glasgow Green.

The half-marathon runners follow an urban route through the city before crossing the River Clyde, going towards Bellahouston and Pollok Country Park and then returning to the city centre.

The 10k follows a more urban course, skipping the park section but taking in four bridges and a long riverside stretch instead.

What road closures will be in place in Glasgow?

A large number of road closures and parking restrictions will be in effect for the event, both on the route itself and surrounding areas around the city.

St Vincent Street, Paisley Road West and part of Argyle Street will be closed until at least the middle of the afternoon.

Full details can be found via a downloadable map on the Great Scottish Run website.

articles.title: Draymond Green says Warriors are ‘different’ this season after Kerr’s promise, ‘It’s delusion…’
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors are focused on avoiding a repeat of last season, and Draymond Green has made a bold promise to the fans, based on Steve Kerr’s comm...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are focused on avoiding a repeat of last season, and Draymond Green has made a bold promise to the fans, based on Steve Kerr's comments.

It has been less than a week or so of practice for the Golden State Warriors, and their core is fighting against Father Time this season.

Jimmy Butler, Steph Curry, Draymond Green, and Al Horford aren't getting any younger, while Kristaps Porzingis can't get off the treatment table.

Having said all that, Green has seen a "different" version of the Warriors already, and it's based on what Kerr told them at the start of this season.

Draymond Green shakes off "delusion" at Golden State Warriors

The Warriors tried to strike big in the market this off-season but ended up empty-handed, leaving them in a precarious position.

Nobody is considering them as playoff locks, let alone title contenders, but experience can't be bought, and the Warriors have plenty of it.

Green is famously demanding of people around him, so it speaks volumes that he has given a glowing verdict on the mood around camp despite the noise outside.

Curry's extension has helped, but what impressed Green the most was how Kerr told them that he let them down last season and is going to change things up now.

He said [via The Draymond Green Show ]: "I've always talked about the leader Coach Kerr is. He started off the meeting like, 'I failed you all last year. I don't think I did a good enough job of having guys ready to go.'

"Boom. Boom. Boom. Then he goes, 'These are the things we are doing'. I'll tell you, the first three days of practice have been different. A lot different. I respect it.

"You can't just have the season we had last year and pick up and do the same thing again. That's delusional. No one around here is delusional. It has been an extremely competitive training camp."

Green named the likes of Al Horford, Will Richards, Graham Ike, and more as players who are all driven to make an impact to right the wrongs of last season.

If they can get their experienced core on the floor reliably, and Porzingis manages to stay fit for the big games, then the Warriors can't be completely written off.

If Green is convinced with the effort of his teammates, then something is going right behind the scenes.

articles.title: Green Party members back 'Zionism is racism' conference motion
articles.summary: The vote has caused divisions among figures at the top of the party at its conference in Brighton.
articles.body:
Green Party members have adopted a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism, in a move that has divided senior figures at the top of the party.

The party's two deputy leaders have been at odds over the subject, with Mothin Ali backing the move, and Rachel Millward describing the wording as "problematic".

Activists endorsed the policy motion, which was put forward by a group of members at the party's conference in Brighton, by 1022 votes to 813.

They also voted to commit the party to supporting a "single democratic Palestinian State", after they rejected an amendment that had been backed by party leader Zack Polanski.

The motion adopted by Green members defines Zionism as an ideology in support of "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and backs a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".

"The real, material, manifestation of Zionism has been the historic and ongoing dehumanisation, displacement, dispossession, disenfranchisement and destruction of Palestinians," it says.

It has attracted criticism from some Jewish groups, including the Board of Deputies and the Jewish Leadership Council.

In a letter to the party sent ahead of the vote, the organisations said Zionism was an anti-racist movement, adding that "modern Zionism was formed in part as a response to antisemitism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it."

It also raised concerns about the safety of Jewish members in the Green Party, as well as the implications for Jewish institutions in areas represented by the Greens.

Debate about the motion, as well as the conflict in Gaza, has featured heavily during the conference, which is taking place after a surge in its membership following Polanski's election as leader last year.

On Friday, Polanski said he believed Zionism, as it was defined in the motion, was racism.

However, he said he wanted to see the reference to a single Palestinian state changed, arguing: "I don't believe we as a Green Party of England and Wales, or even the British government, should be deciding what the future settlement looks like."

He had also said he wanted to see the motion amended to specify that it should not be used to discipline Jewish members attending synagogues that consider themselves Zionist.

However, both amendments favoured by Polanski were rejected by Green members.

A Green spokeswoman insisted the party would protect Jewish members - and they would not be persecuted for attending synagogues which defined themselves as Zionist.

Polanski himself did not vote in the debate, having left the conference early to campaign in Holborn and St Pancras, where he is standing to be the MP. A full list of candidates can be found here.

Over the course of the three-day conference, key figures in the party have expressed differing positions about the Zionism motion.

Three of the party's five MPs - Ellie Chowns, Adrian Ramsay and Carla Denyer - had publicly opposed it, with Denyer arguing it could risk "alienating a significant proportion of Jewish people".

On Friday, former leader Caroline Lucas told the BBC: "I think there is no single definition of Zionism and, irrespective of the intentions of those who put that motion, I think there is a real risk that it will be divisive and could be seen as a sign that Jewish people aren't welcome in the party."

Deputy leader Mothin Ali, who had expressed support for the motion before the vote, said it was calling for "a state that's democratic, that guarantees the rights of every single person living on that land".

He added that he was "absolutely not" calling all Jewish people who define themselves as Zionists racist.

Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, contract talks have broken down between the Detroit Lions and star tight end Sam LaPorta.

A second-round draft pick in 2023, LaPorta burst onto the scene with a standout rookie season. LaPorta had 86 grabs for 889 yards and 10 touchdowns during his rookie campaign in 2023. Then, LaPorta hauled in 60 catches for 726 yards and seven scores in 2024.

LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short after just nine games as he underwent back surgery to repair a fully herniated disk. The 6-foot-3, 245-pound tight end has looked like himself to start this season, registering 14 receptions for 144 yards and a score.

In his career thus far, LaPorta has 200 receptions for 2,248 yards and 21 touchdowns.

LaPorta is represented by agent Jack Bechta, who also represents Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft. Kraft landed a four-year, $75 million contract extension prior to the season. LaPorta was a second-team All-Pro and a Pro Bowler in 2023.

articles.title: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk outlasts Casey Jarvis to claim victory at St Andrews
articles.summary: Adrian Meronk ended a 1,078-day wait to win his fifth DP World Tour Title as he surged past Casey Jarvis to win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship by two shots; watch next week's Open de Espana live on Sky Sports Golf from Thursday at 1pm
articles.body:
The victory saw the LIV Golfer end a 1,078-day wait to claim his fifth DP World Tour title and regain his tour card for next season, as he wrapped up his week with a four-under 68.

Jarvis held a two-stroke lead coming into day four at St Andrews, and following a fast start that included back-to-back birdies on holes four and five, he slumped, making bogeys on holes nine and 11.

A thrilling finish unravelled, with Meronk, who held a two-shot lead going into the final three holes, giving Jarvis a chance to cut the gap on the 17th after the Cleeks GC player carded a bogey.

But Jarvis couldn't reduce the deficit, as the South African missed the green on the penultimate hole and went down for a bogey.

It meant Jarvis would walk down the 18th fairway needing to make an eagle to force a play-off and after finding the fringes of the green with his drive, he was unable to make a long eagle putt, confirming Meronk's victory.

"I never usually cry, but this one feels very special," Meronk said.

"It's been quite a tough year for me, but to win here 10 years after turning pro, it's a dream come true."

Jarvis posted a final round 72 to finish tied for second with Niklas Nørgaard.

World No 979 Michael Stewart enjoyed a fairy tale week at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, as the 36-year-old, who was playing on the Tartan Pro Tour last week, placed tied for fourth with Tommy Fleetwood, at 16-under.

Brooks Koepka earned his first top-10 finish on both the DP World Tour and PGA Tour since March, with the American joining last year's Alfred Dunhill Links champion Robert MacIntyre at 16 under to tie for sixth place.

England's Matthew Jordan, who began the day two shots back from overnight leader Jarvis, endured a day to forget, as he slumped down the leaderboard to tied-11th after he posted a three-over 75 at the Old Course.

Open de France champion Matt Fitzpatrick would also fall down the leaderboard to tied-17th after he wrapped up his final round at level par.

Meronk: I asked Woods and Nicklaus for good energy walking down the 18th

Meronk got his final round off to a flying start, carding back-to-back birdies on his first two holes, before making more gains on the fourth, as he and Jarvis battled for the lead.

He'd cancel out a bogey on the seventh with a birdie on the ninth, before taking the solo lead with a birdie on the 12th and extending his advantage with another on the 14th. From there, he'd hold on to seal victory, despite a bogey on the 17th.

"After my drive on 18, I was quite happy with the position I was in," Meronk said.

"It's an amazing walk when you cross the bridge. You look around: the people, the history.

"Actually, when I was crossing the bridge, I talked to myself. I was thinking about Tiger Woods and Jack Nicklaus walking over the bridge, and I was asking for good energy from them.

"It was a great feeling. I really enjoyed that."

Meronk's victory also saw him become only the third player to win both the individual competition and the team event in the tournament's history, as he and Keane lead singer Tom Chaplin sealed a one-shot victory in the Pro-Am.

Stewart: My focus is on the Tartan Pro Tour

Stewart was "delighted" to finish so high up the leaderboard, with the 36-year-old banking himself a cheque of £168,000 for his tied-fourth finish.

His performance banked him a spot at next week's Open de Espana in Madrid but Stewart, who currently is second on the Tartan Pro Tour's Order of Merit, said he was committed to playing at its next event, the Gleneagles Masters.

Stewart can win himself a HotelPlanner Tour card for 2027 if he finishes second on the Tartan Pro Tour's Order of Merit.

"Definitely, I'm going to have to go play the Tartan Tour next week," Stewart said. "I don't want to be left in limbo with obviously nowhere to play next season after a great season.

"That's where my head is at right now. It's obviously great to have a fantastic week this week. But the focus has to be on the Tartan Tour."

On Wednesday, Michael Stewart earned £2,500 for finishing runner-up in the Tartan Pro Tour event at Duddingston Golf Club near Edinburgh.

Four days later, the world number 979 has just picked up nearly 100 times that by finishing joint fourth behind winner Adrian Meronk at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

But what the 36-year-old Scot regards as "without doubt" the best week of his career has left him with a dilemma.

Finishing in the top 10 - two shots behind Poland's Meronk, one behind Denmark's Niklas Norgaard and South Africa's Casey Jarvis, and tied with England's Tommy Fleetwood - means he qualifies for next week's big-money Spanish Open.

However, that clashes with the conclusion to the Tartan Pro Tour, the Gleneagles Masters, after which Stewart will qualify for next year's second-tier Challenge Tour should he protect his current second place.

"Right now, in all honesty, in my mind, it's definitely play the Tartan Pro Tour final at Gleneagles," Stewart said.

"If I don't go and somebody overtakes me, I don't think that's the right thing to do.

"I've played so well to put myself in that position as well. There's so many good players behind me. One of three or four guys can catch me and, if one of them plays well, they can win.

"It would be silly if I wasn't to go to Gleneagles and at least tee it up and try and secure my Challenge Tour card.

While Meronk was earning his fifth win on the DP World Tour, Stewart, who finished one stroke ahead of compatriot and defending champion Robert MacIntyre, was making only his sixth appearance - having missed the cut in his previous five events.

The Ayrshire-based former Walker Cup player finished joint 52nd at The Open Championship at Royal Liverpool in 2023 but described his performance at Kingsbarns, Carnoustie and St Andrews this week as a career highlight.

"The Open was amazing, but I felt really disheartened after the Sunday at The Open because I felt like I threw away what could have been a really special weekend," he said.

"But this is amazing. It gives yourself a little bit more belief that you can go on and compete at this level."

articles.title: ‘Helping Us Win a Lot of Games’ — Dennis Allen Sets High Expectations for Kyler Gordon’s Return
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon is finally back on the practice field, and the Bears are not hiding how much they still expect from him. Gordon has...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon is finally back on the practice field, and the Bears are not hiding how much they still expect from him.

Gordon has spent most of the season dealing with a calf injury and missed training camp while working away from the team with his own medical and training personnel. Now that he is back, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen made it clear that the Bears still see a significant role for the veteran cornerback once he is ready.

Dennis Allen Sets Clear Standard for Kyler Gordon's Bears Return

The Bears opened Gordon's 21-day practice window this week, giving the team time to evaluate him before deciding when to activate him. He has been a full participant since returning; however, Allen wants to make sure Gordon can handle the demands of playing football again before putting him into a game.

The biggest concern is not Gordon's ability. The defensive coordinator said his confidence in the cornerback has never changed.

"I've got extreme confidence in what he can do when he's on the field, that's never wavered. The biggest thing for Kyler is being able to stay healthy, and that's where our focus is. Once he gets into football shape and stays healthy, I see him getting back on the field and helping us win a lot of games."

Allen also said Gordon looked good during his first work back with the defense. The Bears gave him some extra work on Wednesday, and the coordinator liked what he saw from the way Gordon moved.

Gordon has missed extensive time o ver the past two seasons. A groin injury limited him to three regular-season games and two playoff appearances last year, and the calf issue kept him out of the offseason program, training camp, and the start of this season.

The Bears now have 21 days to decide when he is ready. Allen said the team will use that time to evaluate Gordon's physical condition, with the hope that he can return sooner rather than later.

As for the Bears, getting Gordon back could also change how the secondary is arranged. Rookie Malik Muhammad has taken snaps in the slot while Gordon has been unavailable. Muhammad has shown enough to earn more opportunities, and he also has experience playing outside. That gives the Bears some flexibility if Gordon eventually returns to his familiar nickel role.

Allen has already seen Muhammad step in when needed. With Tyrique Stevenson dealing with a hamstring issue earlier in the week, Muhammad received another opportunity and handled it well.

The CB value goes beyond simply f illing the slot. Allen has used him as a blitzer and can move him around the formation because of his athleticism. The Bears signed him to a three-year, $40M extension in 2024 because they viewed him as an important part of the defense.

Gordon will not play against the Jets this week; however, the Bears can potentially have him available for their Week 5 matchup with the Green Bay Packers.

articles.title: Israel lashes out as UK’s Green Party formally defines Zionism as ‘racism’
articles.summary: Israel’s president declared that the ‘antisemitic lie’ deliberately endangers Jews and Israelis.
articles.body:
Israel has reacted with anger after the United Kingdom’s Green Party voted to define Zionism as a form of racism.

Israel, as well as British Jewish groups, lashed out on Sunday following the vote by the small political party. The Israeli government declared that it now views the left-leaning Greens as giving “legitimacy to terrorism”.

The Green Party, which received 6 percent of the vote in the UK’s national elections in 2024, said ⁠it regarded Zionism as “an ethnonationalist political project” and repeated its call for Britain’s Labour government to end all arms trade with Israel.

In a swift response, Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the policy went “far beyond the boundaries of legitimate political debate” and called on other British political parties to condemn the resolution.

“The Greens have adopted not only the green of Hamas, but also its ideology: the elimination of the State of Israel through armed struggle,” the ministry wrote on social media.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog labelled the move “a disgrace and a shame”. Writing on social media, he said: “Those who claim the antisemitic lie that ‘Zionism is racism’ deliberately endanger Jews and Israelis everywhere.”

Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid said it is “not Zionism that’s racism, it is the Green Party”.

The Movement for Progressive Judaism, a British group, said: “The Green Party has made ⁠antisemitism party policy and become a racist party”.

It added that the support of some Jews for the motion did not mean it would not be used to discriminate against others.

During the vote, the Green Party also reaffirmed its “commitment to Palestinian liberation, the right of return, Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS), and a full arms embargo against Israel”.

It also reiterated support for “the establishment of a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine”, the party said in a statement.

The motion was backed by a majority of 1,022 to 813. Party leader Zack Polanski , who is running for Parliament in former Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s London constituency, did not vote.

In an interview with UK media outlet Sky News, the Greens’ co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said that the heavy casualty toll during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and its ongoing attacks were the context for the vote.

The Green Party has five sitting members in the UK’s 650-seat parliament.

Following the passage of the resolution, Polanski and other Green Party members said in a joint statement they would “continue to stand in opposition to genocide, ethnic cleansing, apartheid and the illegal occupation” and “call out the heinous crimes of the Netanyahu government”.

articles.title: Sean Payton Admits Saints Weren’t Prepared for What Happened Inside Superdome
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints‘ return to the Superdome in 2006 became more than football, and Sean Payton admits even those living through it couldn’t fully underst...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints' return to the Superdome in 2006 became more than football, and Sean Payton admits even those living through it couldn't fully understand what was coming.

Twenty years later, Payton is preparing to revisit that unforgettable night as New Orleans commemorates the anniversary of its first game back in the Superdome following Hurricane Katrina. The Saints will fittingly host the Atlanta Falcons on "Monday Night Football," the same opponent they defeated 23-3 on Sept. 25, 2006, in a game forever connected to the city's recovery.

Payton, now the Denver Broncos' head coach, was asked this week what he remembered about the occasion. His answer offered a fascinating look at just how unusual the buildup was for a Saints team that had spent much of its first season together away from New Orleans.

"I don't know that any player or coach on that team, when everyone kind of got there, could expect what all of it was going to mean," Payton said. "I do remember this though, training camp was away because of facilities. It was a long training camp. It was seven weeks in Jackson, Mississippi."

Sean Payton Couldn't Prepare Saints for Superdome Atmosphere

The Saints weren't simply preparing for another home opener. Payton recalled playing preseason home games in Shreveport and Jackson before opening the regular season with road victories over the Cleveland Browns and Green Bay Packers .

New Orleans and Atlanta both entered the Superdome at 2-0, but the game carried a significance no normal undefeated matchup possibly could. Payton even brought his team into the stadium Friday night to practice under the lights and familiarize itself with a building it had yet to call home that season.

"But even with all that being said, as much as you try as a coach to prepare for what the environment's going to be like, it's hard to do that," Payton said. "So that was unique."

Then came the moment that still defines the night. Steve Gleason blocked Atlanta's first punt, Curtis Deloatch recovered it for a touchdown and the Superdome erupted less than two minutes into the game. New Orleans eventually won 23-3 in front of 70,003 fans.

Payton understood there was symbolism surrounding the reopening, but even he couldn't anticipate what that Saints team would ultimately represent to New Orleans.

"There were so many other people that maybe normally wouldn't be at a Saints game," Payton said. "Then there was a lot of symbolism, obviously, as the first event back there at a place that was literally broken."

That's what makes Payton's reflection resonate 20 years later. Coaches spend their careers preparing for every imaginable situation, but on one of the most important nights in Saints history, there was simply no playbook for what awaited New Orleans inside that building.

Now, 20 years later, the Saints prepare to face the Falcons under those same Superdome lights, with another generation getting a reminder of why that night will forever mean more to New Orleans than football.
